title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (baseline single-shot validity vs final guarded validity after deterministic validation/repair) with gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses). All 200 baseline initial candidates were judged valid by the deterministic validator and no repairs were applied; guarded outcomes therefore matched baseline: baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI 0.00–0.00, exact McNemar p = 1.0). The preregistered power analysis assumed baseline success substantially below 1.0 (target baseline scenarios around p≈0.5); the observed ceiling (baseline=1.0) invalidates those power assumptions and renders the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally targeted 10 percentage‑point improvement. We report the preregistered methodology, execution manifest, exact analysis results, and an evidence-grounded interpretation of this null outcome, and we identify specific next-step preregistered experiments (fault-injection, multi-sample stochastic generation, multi-model comparison) needed to estimate validator coverage and repair utility.

sections.introduction: Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) and agentic workflows are being proposed to translate operator intent into executable network configurations and to automate NetOps workflows. A common architectural safety pattern interposes deterministic validators and repair loops in generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines to bound stochastic generation and reject or repair invalid outputs. Despite growing interest, rigorous, preregistered evaluations of validator coverage and their predictive value for end-to-end guarded success remain scarce. Research question. We preregistered and executed study AC-2026-03 to answer: does a multidimensional validator metric suite (coverage, false-positive/false-negative rates, detection latency, operational-impact proxy) explain more variance in end-to-end agentic NetOps success than a single verifier pass rate? Contributions. (1) A preregistered, machine-readable paired design that isolates downstream validator/repair effects via shared_initial_candidate semantics; (2) a closed execution with exact accounting and archived artifacts; (3) clear reporting of a degenerate (ceiling) confirmatory result and an evidence-grounded discussion showing why this execution could not estimate validator-driven repair benefit; (4) concrete, preregistered next-step experiment prescriptions to avoid the observed ceiling effect.
sections.related_work: Representative prior work motivates verifier layers and GVR-style architectures for reducing mechanically detectable defects and enabling structured repair feedback in code and system settings [1]. Benchmarks and controlled suites for AIOps/NetOps show substantive failure modes—ticket noise, false-premise issues, and wrong-but-plausible outputs—that complicate end-to-end automation and evaluation [2],[3]. Recent proposals advocate self-healing orchestrators, auditable decision traces, and verifier-guided repair to reduce silent failures in tool-augmented LLM systems [4]. These works motivate our measurement focus but leave empirical questions about (a) how to quantify validator coverage and FP/FN behavior in NetOps GVR flows and (b) how validator metrics predict operational-impact proxies; our experiment was designed to address that measurement gap under strict preregistration.
sections.methodology: Design summary. Confirmatory paired design preregistered as AC-2026-03. Adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model: declared_model_version gpt-5-mini (provider bundle 'openai_responses'); task_count=200 pairs (planned_episode_count=400); generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial candidate per task reused for both baseline and guarded conditions). Important preregistered note (archived): model_configuration.temperature was null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; the preregistered power plan targeted detecting an absolute 0.10 (10 percentage-point) paired improvement with alpha=0.05 and ~80% power under conservative baseline scenarios (baseline p values explored in the preregistration included 0.3–0.7). Task bank and validators. Tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 using intent_configuration_repair_v1 payloads (difficulty levels 'very_hard'–'extreme') with explicit allowed-field and required-sequence constraints. The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed full intent-constraint validation and produced a binary validity label plus validator traces (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation codes, repair_applied flag). Execution contract and sampling. The adapter performed exactly one initial generation per task (initial_generation_calls_per_task=1) shared across baseline and guarded; maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1. The execution manifest and raw outputs are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json and referenced artifacts). Analysis plan. Primary test: paired binary outcome analysis (exact two-sided McNemar), with bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed=1729) as preregistered. Secondary summaries (registered but exploratory) included per-validator FP/FN summaries and detection-latency distributions where estimable.
sections.results: Execution accounting. The run completed per preregistration: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, model_calls_used=200 (one shared initial generation per pair), failed_episode_count=0. Confirmatory outcome. Baseline_success_count = 200/200, guarded_success_count = 200/200. Paired contingency: n_11=200, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0; paired difference = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000). Validator/repair behavior. For every task the validator trace recorded valid=true and repair_applied=false; no repair prompts were issued because the shared initial candidates satisfied the validator's intent-constraint checks. Consequence for inferential power. The preregistered power analysis assumed non-degenerate baseline success (examples used baseline p≈0.5 and sensitivity for baseline p in {0.3,0.4,0.5,0.6,0.7}); the observed baseline success rate = 1.0 violates those assumptions (ceiling effect). As a result the primary confirmatory design could not detect the preregistered 10 percentage‑point improvement—the test is uninformative under complete ceiling. Secondary metrics. Per-validator FP/FN/latency distributions are degenerate here (no observed false negatives or false positives). Representative artifacts. Representative episode responses, validator traces, and the exact execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl).
sections.discussion: Interpretation. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, baseline measures the single-shot validity of the shared initial candidate; guarded measures final validity after any permitted validator-triggered repair. The null result therefore indicates that, for the specific synthetic task bank, model, and sampled seeds, the generator produced initial candidates that already satisfied the deterministic validator's mechanistic intent-constraint checks. Scientifically, this outcome does not imply GVR pipelines lack value generally; rather it highlights three determinants of measured validator utility: (1) task/fault prevalence and targeted fault-injection, (2) generator sampling regime (single shared sample vs multi-sample stochastic draws), and (3) validator coverage (mechanical checks vs semantic intent alignment). Practical lessons and next-step preregistered experiments. To estimate validator coverage and repair utility we recommend a follow-up preregistered confirmatory design that (A) injects targeted faults into a pre-specified fraction of task instances (syntactic, configuration-logic, and semantic intent-mismatch classes) so that baseline validity is below ceiling; (B) uses multi-sample stochastic generation per task (e.g., k≥3 independent draws) to measure generator variability; and (C) includes at least two model families and at least one alternative validator implementation to probe external validity. Under such a design the paired estimand should be reframed (or supplemented) so that guarded improvements can result either from validator-triggered repair or from accepting a different valid sampled candidate. Reproducibility and artifact pointers. All preregistration, execution manifests, raw outputs, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the supplied artifact bundle).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory study under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR flows. For the selected synthetic task bank and gpt-5-mini sampled seeds, every initial candidate passed the deterministic validator; consequently no repairs occurred and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeting a 10 percentage‑point improvement from a baseline near p≈0.5) were invalidated by the observed ceiling (baseline=1.0), rendering the primary inferential test uninformative for the originally planned effect. This result emphasizes that rigorous validator evaluation requires targeted fault-injection, stochastic multi-sample generation, and multi-model/validator comparisons. We present the archived artifacts and recommend the described next-step preregistered designs to estimate validator FP/FN behavior and repair utility in operationally meaningful conditions. REFERENCES are provided after the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure (concise). Model and provider: declared model gpt-5-mini via provider bundle 'openai_responses'. Orchestration/adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family and approved the master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI system autonomously performed literature review, preregistration (AC-2026-03), execution, analysis, internal review, and manuscript drafting without manual editing of technical content. Master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Sampling and generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). Model configuration note: execution/model_configuration.json recorded temperature as null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Call budget and usage (preregistered): maximum_model_calls=400; actual model_calls_used=200 (one shared initial generation per pair). Preregistration preceded execution; all raw outputs, validator traces, execution manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied execution bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json). No human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate; only downstream validator/repair could create paired differences.
The synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was used; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded model_configuration.temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in the execution manifest.
